subject: AWS Marketplace: seller enablement, metering & SaaS fulfillment next steps
snippet: Working with AWS to finalize metering and SaaS fulfillment wiring for Acme deal; internal checklist and contract items called out.
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@amazon.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace seller onboarding & metering — Acme (RDW-ACME-2025-Q4)

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the intro last week. We want to move Acme Corp to an AWS-billed SaaS offering (metered usage + monthly invoice reconciliation) and need to confirm the integration path for:

- SaaS entitlement mapping (how AWS identifies Acme seats/entitlements vs. our internal customer ids)
- Metering reports and timelines (POST usage calls, delta vs cumulative, reporting window)
- Fulfillment contract signing and who signs the SAAS/Marketplace contract (Redwood or Acme)
- Any required webhook endpoints or IP allowlists for the marketplace fulfillment notifications

I've attached a short checklist and a payload example for the entitlement event we can emit. Can you confirm the recommended metering API (Consumption Metering vs SaaS Entitlement API) for our flow and the typical timeline to enable a paid offer after we submit the seller listing?

Cc'ing Laura (legal) and Monica (finance) to surface contract and invoicing constraints up front. Dylan from product is on the integration details.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@amazon.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Seller Support <aws-marketplace-seller-support@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace seller onboarding & metering — Acme (RDW-ACME-2025-Q4)

Hi Karthik — great to connect. Short answers up front, then a few action items.

1) Entitlement model: For SaaS multi-tenant SaaS where the buyer is billed by AWS and the vendor receives payout, we typically use the SaaS Marketplace Entitlements API + the Fulfillment Integration. Entitlements map to the AWS buyer account (buyerAccountId) and you can also pass an externalCustomerId for your mapping.

2) Metering: Use the AWS SaaS Metering API (MeterUsage) for metered dimensions (units), and report once per billing period or with near real-time events depending on your latency tolerance. MeterUsage accepts a productCode, dimension, and quantity; it must be idempotent for retries.

3) Contract: For Acme, if they want AWS-billing (recommended), the buyer accepts the AWS Marketplace offer and AWS handles invoicing. Redwood signs the seller agreement with AWS; Acme signs terms via AWS UI. If Acme requires a separate commercial contract, that can be a private addendum.

4) Webhooks & IPs: The fulfillment flow uses SNS notifications for subscriptions and entitlement changes; you should provide an HTTPS endpoint with a valid cert and allowlist AWS SNS IP ranges.

Action items for Redwood:
- Provide example entitlement payload (you already attached — good).
- Confirm productCode and dimensions you will register.
- Share a public endpoint for SNS (or confirm we'll use SQS + IAM role).

I'll open a seller enablement ticket and assign an enablement engineer who will run a pre-prod validation. Expect ~5 business days to enable the offer after we have productCode and test endpoints.

Samir
AWS Marketplace

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: AWS Marketplace seller onboarding & metering — Acme (RDW-ACME-2025-Q4)

Forwarding Samir's note. Key internal asks distilled:

1) Product code + dimensions: Dylan — propose two dimensions: "inference_tokens" (per-1k tokens) and "dedicated_instances_hours" (per-hour). We need to register these with AWS and confirm idempotency handling.

2) Endpoints: Ops will stand up an SNS HTTPS endpoint for notifications. Monica — finance, does AWS billing cadence (monthly with 45-day payout lag) align with Acme's procurement requirements? If not, we'll need a private addendum.

3) Contract: Laura — please advise whether Redwood can sign the standard AWS Seller Agreement or if procurement requires specific addenda for Acme.

Attachments: aws_seller_onboarding_checklist.pdf, SaaS_Entitlement_Payload_Example.json

Thanks — Karthik

On Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 1:08 PM Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@amazon.com> wrote:
> Hi Karthik — great to connect...

--
Karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS Marketplace seller onboarding & metering — Acme (RDW-ACME-2025-Q4)

Thanks for the summary. A few legal flags to note:

- Revenue recognition: If Acme prefers AWS invoicing directly, ensure our contracts and revenue team can ingest the AWS payout report. Monica, will we be able to reconcile via the AWS Seller Payout CSV?

- Data residency: Acme has an EU presence but the purchase will be through their US entity. Confirm required data residency statements in the offer listing.

- Indemnity & liability caps: The standard AWS Seller Agreement contains mutual indemnities; if Acme's procurement requires higher liability caps or a hold harmless clause we need a redline path.

Action: I'll draft a short addendum template that we can attach to the offer as a private contract if needed. Meanwhile, request Samir to confirm whether a private terms flow is supported for this offer.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS Marketplace seller onboarding & metering — Acme (RDW-ACME-2025-Q4)

Quick finance check:

- AWS payouts: yes, we can reconcile via the Seller Payout CSVs but need to map productCode -> our internal sku for GL mapping. Please ensure productCode is stable.
- Payout timing: AWS usually pays net-45 after month end. If Acme requires vendor invoicing on a different cadence, we will need a private addendum or a 3rd-party marketplace arrangement.
- Taxes: For US buyers, sales tax handling varies by state; for Acme (US entity) we likely clear as marketplace-facilitated in most states but will confirm.

Action: Dylan/Karthik — please provide final productCode and a provisional SKU mapping table.

Monica
Head of RevOps, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace seller onboarding & metering — Acme (RDW-ACME-2025-Q4)

Thanks everyone — quick status update and next steps:

- Dylan: please finalize dimensions and pick a stable productCode by Monday 11/10. Proposed working productCode: RDW-ACME-2025.
- Ops: I'll provision an HTTPS SNS endpoint in staging and share the URL (or SQS + IAM role) with Samir for testing.
- Laura: appreciate the addendum draft — once ready, we'll attach as a private contract link for Acme if procurement needs it.
- Monica: I'll include a SKU mapping CSV in the next message.

Samir — can your enablement ticket include a pre-prod test window next week (11/11-11/14)? If we have productCode and a staging endpoint by 11/10 we should be able to run the validation in that window. Also confirm whether we should use MeterUsage for tokens or a custom dimension.

Attaching: Redwood_AWS_Fulfillment_Playbook.docx (internal runbook).

Thanks — Karthik
